description:
FILED s451w, found by the #685 review probes.  PRE-EXISTING (measured on the
718db6b base tree as well as after #685); #685 fixed the FOREIGN-qualified
half of it by accident (`%{"foo::ENV"}` no longer touches main's), the
main-qualified and unqualified spellings still clobber.

MECHANISM.  The runtime keeps %ENV and %INC as MARKER symbols, not hash
tables: `%ENV` is bound to the symbol `%ENV-MARKER%` and every hash primitive
(p-hash-get / p-hash-set / p-keys / p-exists / p-delete / the iterator) has an
arm for it that talks to the real process environment.  `%p-symref-hash` does

    (unless (and (boundp sym) (hash-table-p (symbol-value sym)))
      (setf (symbol-value sym) (make-hash-table :test 'equal)))

so the first `%{"main::ENV"}` REPLACES the marker with an empty hash table --
and from then on %ENV is an ordinary empty hash for the rest of the process:
`$ENV{PATH}` is undef, `keys %ENV` is 0, and a child inherits nothing PCL set.
`%p-symref-array` has the identical shape but no marker-valued array is known,
so only the hash half is reachable today.

MEASURED (s451w probe p685b, PCL vs perl):
    $ENV{PCLPROBE} = "yes"; $INC{"zz.pm"} = "zz";
    print exists ${"main::ENV"}{PCLPROBE} ? "shared" : "separate";
        perl: shared     PCL: separate   (and %ENV is now empty)
    print exists ${"main::INC"}{"zz.pm"} ? "shared" : "separate";
        perl: shared     PCL: separate

FIX SHAPE: `%p-symref-hash` must not treat "not a hash-table" as "not
initialised".  The marker IS the hash, and every consumer of the value already
knows the marker (p-cast-% hands markers on unchanged), so the guard should be
"replace only when the binding is unbound or holds something that is neither a
hash-table nor a known hash MARKER" -- and per CLAUDE.md rule 12, a bound value
that is neither should DIE naming the name and the value rather than being
silently discarded, because the value it discards is one the program then
consumes.  Grep `%ENV-MARKER%` / `%INC-MARKER%` for the marker set; there is
already a predicate-shaped test at p-hash-clear (`(when (or (eq h '%ENV-MARKER%)
(eq h '%INC-MARKER%)) â¦)`) -- rule 11 says extract that one test rather than
writing a second copy here.

BAR: the two probe rows above identical to perl; `%ENV = (a=>1)` (the
list-assignment arm, which already special-cases the marker) unchanged; a
guard row in Pl/t/symref-package-01.t; sweep + the op/ + io/ companion legs
(a cl/ change).  NOTE the probe hazard this creates: any probe file that reads
`%{"main::ENV"}` before the fix silently empties %ENV for everything after it.

RULED s451 (Fable, 2026-08-29, W ask 3): DIE-shaped.  A bound value that is neither a hash-table nor a known hash MARKER means %p-symref-hash and the binding disagree about what the symbol holds, and the discarded value FLOWS ONWARD (the caller consumes the vivified hash) -- rule 12 boundary test says die naming the symbol and the value TYPE.  The marker set lives in p-hash-clear; the fix must ask ONE shared marker predicate (rule 11), not copy the list.
CLOSED s451z, die-shaped as ruled.  ONE marker predicate
`%p-hash-marker-p` (rule 11): the membership test existed twice already, at
p-gethash-box and in the `each` iterator, and %p-symref-hash was a third site
that had forgotten it.  A binding that is neither a table, a marker nor
undef/NIL DIES naming the symbol and the value's TYPE.

`%p-symref-array` deliberately keeps its shape (no MARKER-valued array
exists); its comment says so and points at the hash twin.

PROBED vs 5.40.3, 17 rows, all identical after: `%{"main::ENV"}` and
`%{"main::INC"}` shared, the unqualified `%{"ENV"}` spelling, a write through
the symref, delete, each, keys, `%ENV = (â¦)`, and the #685 inverse
(`%{"foo::ENV"}` stays foo's own and leaves the environment alone).

Guard Pl/t/symref-package-01.t rows 14-15.  A `cl/` change, so the batch's
sweep and the op/ + io/ companion legs are the merge review's.
subject: `%{"main::ENV"}` (and `%{"ENV"}`, `%{"main::INC"}`) DESTROYS the process environment -- %p-symref-hash sees the %ENV-MARKER% binding is not a hash-table and REPLACES it with a fresh empty one
